decisions.decision: Closure = 4× 4×2 N35 magnet pairs (NOT 5×2, NOT M3 bolts)
decisions.rationale: Lid is ~120 g of PETG. Alignment tab handles shear. 4 pairs × ~300 g pull each = ~1.2 kg holding force, 5–10× margin under rally vibration. Tool-free service.

decisions.decision: Alignment feature lives on TRAY, not upper
decisions.rationale: Tray prints floor-down naturally — tab is the last feature laid down, in open air, no overhang. On the upper it would have been a fragile first-layer feature when printed seam-down (the natural orientation for the castle features).
Clean 2-perimeter extrusion on a 0.4 mm nozzle. 0.6 was right at the 1.5-perimeter limit. Costs 0.2 mm of cavity per wall — invisible vs PI5_INSET=3.5.
Magnets only fight lift-off; tab handles shear. Tab on the easy-print side means we can afford the taller feature for ~2× lateral resistance.
Pointed-arch crown is a PETG overhang at the worst possible spot (the open mouth). Lid plate already spans the gatehouse top, so structurally redundant. Module left defined for revert.

43 mm decorative ring centred at z=51.5 dipped 3 mm below the seam (z=30), forcing supports under the upper print. Fan APERTURE and mounting screw holes remain in pi_case_fan_cutout — fan still works, just no decorative ring.
From prior session — kept. 3.4 mm margin between Pi standoff boss and tower centre. Now also hosts the 4.1 mm magnet pockets with 3.95 mm of PETG sleeve around each.
